descs: Salt marsh and gray water, wind carrying the smell of iron and old fish.

spots.name: The Coast Path
spots.desc: The path drops toward Gullhaven's roofs and the smell of woodsmoke. Inland, the marsh opens out, salt and gray water as far as the eye finds a stopping place.

actions.label: size up the path as a soldier would
fx: One archer here could hold this whole path against a dozen. The brush is already cleared for a clean shot, north side. Somebody thought of it before you did.

spots.name: The Point
spots.desc: The headland ends here, cliffs dropping to a hidden shingle beach below. Out past the rocks, fog sits low on the water even when the rest of the sky runs clear.
spots.brief: The headland's end; a beach below.
onEnterOnce: Oars. Faint, and out of time with any current, somewhere in that fog. You don't see the boat they belong to.

actions.label: ask what Tamsin makes of the oars
fx: Tamsin's hand goes to her belt-knife without seeming to notice. 'Steel doesn't row itself,' she says. 'Whatever's out there, I'd rather trust my blade than my nerve.'

spots.name: Lighthouse Rise
spots.desc: The ground climbs toward a squat stone tower, dark even at noon. Its lamp hasn't turned in longer than anyone in Gullhaven cares to say.
spots.brief: The rise climbs to a dark tower.

actions.label: ask Vell what she makes of the tower
fx: Vell looks up at the dark tower a long while. 'Towers like that don't go dark by accident,' she says. 'They go dark on purpose, and somebody always knows why.'

spots.name: The Beached Longboat
spots.desc: A longboat lies broken-backed on the sand, ribs picked bare by weather and worse. Old pitch still cakes the seams, and something glints deep in the wreckage.
spots.brief: A broken longboat, old pitch in its seams.

actions.label: search the ribs for salvage (wits)
fx: Wedged under a broken thwart: a whole haul of good netting, salt-stiff but sound. Someone stashed this here and never came back.
Sand and old rope, nothing more you can find by feel alone.

actions.label: strip pitch from the hull
fx: The old caulking peels away in a long black strip, still tacky under the salt crust. It'll burn.

spots.name: Samphire Bank
spots.desc: Sea samphire grows thick in the wet ground here, salt-sharp and good against a wound, if you know to eat it raw.

spots.name: The Tide Pools
spots.desc: Rock pools hold the sea in miniature — crabs, anemones, a starfish gone the color of old rust.

actions.label: ask Osk to read the pools
fx: Osk crouches at the water's edge a long while. 'Still water holds still grief,' he says, and doesn't explain further, but he looks steadier for having looked.

spots.name: Cliff Path
spots.desc: The path narrows along the cliff edge, spray reaching up from the rocks below. One wrong step and the sea decides the rest.
spots.brief: A narrow cliff path, spray below.

actions.label: read the claim-marks in the chalk
fx: Chalk marks low on the rock, renewed every season: panner families marking who works which stretch. Watch and Free Companies both leave the custom alone. Cheaper than a war over salt.

spots.name: Salt Pan Flats
spots.desc: Shallow pans catch the tide and let it go, leaving salt in white rings. Herons stand in the runnels, patient as debt.

actions.label: let Vell read the herons
fx: Vell watches the herons a moment. 'Patient as debt,' she says, echoing the pans themselves. 'Everything here is owed to something. The birds included.'

spots.name: Sunken Causeway
spots.desc: An old stone causeway runs half underwater, its far end lost in reeds. Something built this before Gullhaven had a name.

actions.label: read the carved stone (wits)
fx: Under the moss, a spiral cut deep enough to have outlasted the language it was written in. Whatever raised this causeway wasn't building it for anyone in Gullhaven.
The moss won't give up its stone without a knife, and today you haven't got one to spare on it.

spots.name: Kelp Line
spots.desc: A tide-line of kelp and rope-ends marks the last big storm, three seasons gone by the smell of it still.

actions.label: reckon the storm-line's worth
fx: Rope-ends worth salvaging, if anyone still owned them. Three seasons on, the owners are either paid off already or past caring. You'd guess the latter.

spots.name: Bramble Hollow
spots.desc: A hollow out of the wind, brambles heavy with fruit gone sour from the salt air. Something has been feeding here.

actions.label: read what's been feeding here
fx: Not deer. The prints are wrong for it, low and wide, and they favor one back leg. Whatever it is, it's been coming here longer than one season.

spots.name: Salt-Crust Flat
spots.desc: The ground here is crusted white and hard as bone, cracked into a thousand plates that shift underfoot like broken crockery.

actions.label: cross the flat — fail costs 1hp (grace)
fx: The crust holds, barely, each step a small held breath. You're across before it can decide otherwise.
The crust gives all at once and swallows your leg to the knee. Getting free costs more than the mud takes.

spots.name: Reed Cut
spots.desc: Reeds taller than a man, cut back in narrow lanes by hands that knew exactly where they were going.

actions.label: let Tamsin read the cut lanes
fx: Tamsin runs a thumb along one cut reed. 'Fresh, and cut clean — a blade kept sharp on purpose.' She doesn't say it admiringly. She doesn't say it any other way either.

spots.name: Marram Dunes
spots.desc: Marram grass holds the dunes together against a wind that never quite stops. Rabbit tracks cross every slope.

spots.name: Bladderwrack Shingle
spots.desc: Bladderwrack pops underfoot, black and slick. Something has dragged a heavy net through here and not come back for it.

actions.label: follow the drag-marks (wits)
fx: The drag ends at a stripped patch of shingle: rope and a coil of good netting, dumped in a hurry and never reclaimed. Whoever took it left faster than they came.
The weed's too thick and the tide's already blurred the rest of the track.

spots.name: The Spit
spots.desc: A long spit of shingle runs out toward open water, gulls working its whole length, wind scouring every loose thing off it.

variants.desc: A long spit of shingle runs toward open water. The reef beyond sits quiet now, fog thinned to nearly nothing.
variants.brief: A shingle spit; the reef sits quiet.

variants.desc: A long spit of shingle runs toward open water. Smoke still ghosts the reef beyond, thin and going thinner.
variants.brief: A shingle spit; smoke ghosts the reef.

actions.label: cross the spit — fail costs 1hp (grace)
fx: You keep the ridge without the wind deciding for you, and the whole bay opens out: Gullhaven, the reef, the dark lighthouse standing over both.
The wind picks the moment you're balanced worst, and the shingle takes your knees on the way down.

spots.name: The Widow Rocks
spots.desc: Black rocks break the surf offshore, named for every boat that never came back around them. The tide talks to itself here.
spots.brief: Black rocks, named for old wrecks.

actions.label: let Osk name the rocks' dead
fx: Osk reads the rocks' names under his breath, one by one, the way a man says a rite he's said before. 'Somebody should,' he says, when he notices you watching.

spots.name: Fisherman's Cairn
spots.desc: A cairn of flat stones, raised for someone the sea kept. Fresh shells sit on top, left by hands that still remember.

actions.label: leave a shell on the cairn
fx: You set a shell among the others. One more hand that still remembers, whether the sea notices or not.
Osk: 'Small rites keep. That's most of what they're for.'

spots.name: The Watch Cairn
spots.desc: A cairn taller than the rest, stones added by generations of fishermen putting off from this exact spot. Superstition, mostly.
spots.brief: A tall cairn, a fisherman's habit.

actions.label: search beneath the cairn (wits)
fx: Oilskin-wrapped, wedged under the base stone: coin that never once saw a manifest. Whoever hid it trusted the cairn's own name to keep the Watch from looking twice.
Sound stone, close-set. If something's under there, it isn't giving itself up today.

spots.name: The Mudflats
spots.desc: Mudflats stretch out at low tide, pocked with worm-casts and one print of something that walked here on two legs, then stopped.

actions.label: follow the two-legged print (wits)
fx: The print goes three strides toward open water, then simply stops, as if whatever made it left the ground entirely. Pressed into its last hollow: a corroded button, an anchor stamped in it.
The tide's already softening the print's edges. Whatever left it, the ground won't say more today.

spots.name: Low Marsh
spots.desc: The ground goes soft and treacherous, black water standing between hummocks of grass. Better to know the path than guess it.

actions.label: read the palisade's blind side
fx: The wreckers built their palisade facing the tideline and forgot the marsh at their back. One soldier's eye is all it takes to see the whole camp differently.

spots.name: Driftwood Reach
spots.desc: Bleached driftwood piles against a low dune, sorted by hand into stacks — someone here plans to build something, or burn it.

actions.label: search the driftwood stacks (wits)
fx: Each stack is bound with the same quick knot Rennick's crews favor on the quay. Someone's stockpiling here on Company time, and a few coins fell out of the bargain.
Good wood, carefully sorted, and nothing hidden in it that a search alone will find.

spots.name: The Weir
spots.desc: A fish-weir of woven withies stretches across a tidal channel, half its lattice torn away by something stronger than a fish.

actions.label: reach the weir — fail costs 1hp (might)
fx: A decent catch still tangled in the withies, and coin enough with it to make the reach worth the cold.
Something in the weeds still has teeth, torn lattice or not, and it finds your hand before you find the catch.

spots.name: The Gull Colony
spots.desc: Thousands of gulls nest in the marsh grass, and every one of them minds you passing. The noise alone could wake the dead.
spots.brief: Gulls enough to wake the dead.

actions.label: brave the gulls — fail costs 1hp (grace)
fx: You keep low and steady, and the colony judges you not worth the effort of mobbing. Small mercy, loudly delivered.
The colony disagrees, all at once, and you come out the far side with a bleeding scalp and a new respect for gulls.

onEnter: A figure rises out of the reeds ahead, iron bar in hand, sizing up what you're carrying.

sk_lighthouse.name: The Farlight
sk_lighthouse.desc: The lamp room at the tower's top, glass panes salt-blind, the great lens dark. The winding gear sits seized with rust. From up here the whole bay shows: Gullhaven, the reef, and the fog that never quite leaves the point.
sk_lighthouse.brief: The dark lamp room, seized gear.
onEnterOnce: A keeper's logbook lies open on the sill, its last entry unfinished. The ink just stops, mid-word.

variants.desc: The lamp room at the tower's top, its great lens finally turning again, throwing a slow white beam out over the reef. From up here the whole bay shows clean.
variants.brief: The lamp turns; a white beam over the reef.

actions.label: read the keeper's logbook
fx: Weeks of ordinary weather, then one line in a shaking hand: 'Paid well. Told them the glass was fouled. God forgive the reef what I've done to it tonight.' Nothing after.

actions.label: wrench the seized crank around (might)
fx: Rust shears away under your grip and the gear gives all at once, the lens grinding into its slow turn. Light spills out over the water for the first time in a generation.
The crank won't budge, and your hands are raw for the trying.

actions.label: coax the old lens back onto true (grace)
fx: Working blind between the housing and the frame, you ease the lens back onto its track a hair at a time until it simply turns. Light spills out over the water.
The lens shifts, catches, and won't turn true. Not yet.

actions.label: puzzle out the keeper's old drill (wits)
fx: The logbook's routine comes clear: prime, prime again, then turn against the seize, not with it. The gear surrenders exactly where a keeper's hands would have known to push. Light spills out over the water.
Whatever the trick was, the log doesn't say it plainly enough to guess.

actions.label: prime the lamp and touch it off
fx: Fresh oil takes to the old wick at once. The gear, freed of its dry seize, turns almost gently. Light spills out over the water.

actions.label: get your bearings from the Farlight
fx: Gullhaven's quay far south-west; St. Mara's shrine south-west below, the salt-panner's hut west of it; the wreckers' roost south-east; the Weeping Caves east; the hidden shingle at the far south-east end of the coast.

actions.label: swear you'll tend it true (will)
fx: You say it plain, half to the room and half to whatever's left of the keeper who couldn't: this light won't go dark on your watch. Your hands steady around the mechanism, and it turns.
The words are easy enough to say. Getting the gear to believe them is another matter tonight.

sk_samphire.name: sea samphire
sk_samphire.hint: eat it raw to ease a wound

fx: Salt-sharp and bitter, but the ache dulls.

sk_naval_button.name: a corroded naval button
sk_naval_button.hint: an anchor stamped in it — Reeve's fleet issue

sk_snare_cord.name: a coil of snare-wire
sk_snare_cord.hint: good wire, still coiled tight; someone's rabbit-line, abandoned

sk_wrecker_scout.name: wrecker scout
sk_wrecker_scout.desc: Rag-wrapped and quick, an iron bar for a weapon and a wrecker's eye for what you're carrying.
onDeath: The scout drops the bar and goes down still reaching for it. Two coins roll loose from a torn pocket.

vars.NAME: the Weeping Caves
vars.SIGN: Salt has crusted the rock in white rings, high-water marks from tides long past.

vars.NAME: Sela's Hut
vars.SIGN: Net-floats strung on a line click together whenever the sea wind finds the door.
vars.LOOT: a net-float carved like a gull
vars.VOICE: Wind's in the floats. Means weather, or company. You're the company.

vars.NAME: the Wreckers' Roost
vars.SIGN: A cracked ship's bell hangs by the gate, rung once for every wreck Grael's crew has stripped bare.
vars.LOOT: a drowned captain's spyglass, the lens gone milky with salt

vars.NAME: St. Mara's Shrine
vars.SIGN: A ship's lantern hangs dead by the door, its glass salt-fogged past seeing through.
